title: Traffic slicing priority queue with credit pools for tier-aware routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tier-aware traffic slicing component that enforces quota-aware prioritization across Free, Paid, and Enterprise tiers. Introduce per-tenant credit pools, a priority queueing policy with soft-degradation and bounded bursting, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when quotas are low or capacity constrained. The feature must integrate with existing routing/policy engine, be observable in Console, and support staged rollouts and feature flags.
background: Current tier routing is static: requests are routed only by tier tag and capacity pools. When a paid tenant exhausts quota or a free tier surges, we either reject requests or fall back to region-level throttling, causing poor UX and unpredictable cost. We need a quota-aware prioritization layer that smooths spikes, enables controlled bursts, and preserves enterprise SLAs while allowing paid/free differentiation.
goals: Ensure Enterprise traffic maintains high priority with guaranteed minimal capacity during contention
Allow Paid tier to borrow short bursts from a bounded credit pool before hard throttling
Provide graceful degradation paths: degrade model variant -> reduce tokens -> fall back to queued delivery
Expose metrics and tooling for cost impact, queue depth, credit consumption, and fairness
Implement safe rollout with canary by tenant cohorts and kill-switch feature flags
scope: Runtime-level routing policy: credit pools, priority queues, and burst windows
Integration hooks with tenant quota accounting service and billing signals
Console dashboards: credit usage, queue latencies, and per-tier QoS SLOs
Fallback model selection policy and runtime compatibility check
out_of_scope: Billing UI changes to charge for bursts (billing decision handled separately)
Rewriting KV cache behavior or batching algorithms
Cross-region model replication (we only route/select variants, not replicate models)
design_decisions: Use per-tenant credit pool with time-decayed replenishment rather than token-bucket per-request to allow smoother bursts
Implement three priority queues: enterprise > paid > free. Within paid, requests with sufficient credits are treated preferentially
Enforce an admission controller that runs before kernel scheduling to avoid wasted work on requests that will be dropped
Fallback order: same-model quantized variant -> cheaper architecture-compatible variant -> queued delivery with callback
Default burst window: 30s with max burst credits configurable per-customer tier and overridable by dedicated capacity contracts
tradeoffs: Credit pools permit short bursts but complicate fairness calculations across tenants; mitigated with configurable ceilings and telemetry
Admission controller improves efficiency but introduces an extra RPC/lookup (cache the small footprint in node-local store to reduce latency)
Fallback to cheaper variants can change output quality — must be signaled in response metadata and surfaced to customers via Console
Soft-degradation preserves availability but may increase unit cost if we route to more expensive regions/models when local capacity exhausted
implementation_steps: Spec: finalize credit pool semantics and API (Aisha) - 2d
Proto: add admission control hooks in router and define queue interfaces - 3d
Runtime: implement priority queue and credit accounting in serving runtime (Marcus) - 7d
Policy: add fallback model selection module with compatibility matrix - 3d
Integration: wire quota service events and billing signals - 2d
Console: implement dashboards and per-tenant credit visualization - 4d
E2E tests: simulate surge scenarios, credits exhaustion, and fallback correctness - 3d
Canary rollout: enable for internal tenants -> beta customers -> gradual ramp - 3d
acceptance_criteria: Enterprise requests maintain p95 latency within existing SLO under 3x paid+free surge in same zone
Paid tier can sustain configured burst window without immediate hard throttle; credits decrement and replenish as documented
Fallback model variants are selected when credits are insufficient and are reflected in response.metadata.fallback_reason
No silent request drops: all rejections must return standard error with visible reason and customer-facing guidance
Console surfaces credit pool consumption, queue depth, and per-tier dropout rates
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate: default off for hosted; opt-in for Dedicated and Private via config
Phase 1 (internal): enable for infra and SRE tenants, observe metrics for 48h
Phase 2 (beta): enable for 5 low-risk paid customers with active monitoring and rollback playbook
Phase 3 (ramp): enable by percentage for paid plans and limited capacity for free tenants
Phase 4: full general availability with telemetry alert thresholds and docs
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert when paid-tier credit depletion rate > 80% across >= 10 tenants in 5m window
Alert when queue p95 > 2s for enterprise tier
Dashboards: per-tenant credit trend, queue latency per-tier, fallback rate by model variant
Audit logs: admission decisions, fallback triggers, and credit-topup events
